title: What are we using for music creation/refinement?
author: Odd-Fun-1482
selftext:
Nearly all websites and models ive tried make highly orchestrated composed songs, likely because a lot of the training material was record label radio music.

I've had some luck with SUNO in the past, but since their new model (and killing all old models) everything is sounding too industry.  

What's your workflow of your music like?

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Suno is the be-all, end-all for me. 

I have ChatGPT invent made-up lyrics that are just phonemes that are appropriate for the beat and emotional tenor of the song (I call it songskrit) and go ham. 

  
Nothing else comes close to what Suno can do, so if you don't like Suno there's not really any generative solution for you. I've literally tried them all. I download the latest open models that will fit on my hardware the day they are released. 

It's all garbage. 

Suno is the only high quality music generator, which is exactly why the music industry is so violently attacking it.

comments.author: TheVoyant
comments.body:
I write the instrumental (or use an old one) and then feed it into Suno on a custom trained model, I slide the audio influence and styles both up 100%, click MAX and then steer with the style prompt what level variance I want.

Examples:  
[https://suno.com/s/skfNR8BWUzr1cBXO](https://suno.com/s/skfNR8BWUzr1cBXO)  
[https://suno.com/s/wXwlr6rQSM6rs6Wh](https://suno.com/s/wXwlr6rQSM6rs6Wh)

I find all Ai works best when you try to match 1:1 Human/Ai, and I think even basic level instrumentals can do a lot for people. The original versions should be accessible via the links as well lmk if not, lets you see the before and after.

If anyone needs help, always down to remix/experiment with what people have to try and help steer their results for what you intend.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
Udio is good at taking your own lyrics and allowing you to experiement without writing out the whole song in the free version. Ai lyrics have the tendency to be very systematic with the same few key rhymes, so it's best to avoid it in my opinion.

Just take thirty seconds and see if you like the two tracks it produces. Additionally, I like to take the additional track I don't like and cut a section of the track I enjoy with a new prompt and then re-prompt, using that section for dramatically different directions. 

The Udio free version also lets you use most of the tools, including the "style" mode, which helps keep a consistent theme among the subsequent tracks you produce. For example if you make a track you like, save the style, and the next track will be very similar.

There's also a slider which defines the context of a songs length, or, position in that song. This works in tandem with another slider which affects how the prompt strength is defined.

Additionally, you can use the lyrics field with only brackets, and it will attempt to write a command based on the content of the brackets. I usually use this to write in additional prompting for the section, like BRIDGE or VERSE or GUITAR SOLO (etc) It's also very fun to experiment with.
